overall_summary: Crypto markets took a heavy hit today as Bitcoin ETFs saw massive outflows and over a billion dollars in liquidations swept through the space. Bitcoin is hovering near 59,000 in a clear risk-off environment, with hawkish Fed comments adding to the pressure. Overall sentiment remains firmly negative for traders.

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs See $691M Outflows in Single Day
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded their largest daily redemptions of June so far, with roughly 691 million dollars flowing out on Thursday. Funds like Fidelity's FBTC and BlackRock's IBIT led the exits, extending a multi-day streak of withdrawals. Traders should watch this closely because sustained institutional selling can amplify downside moves in BTC price action.
items.impact: Adds selling pressure and weighs on near-term sentiment

items.title: Over $1 Billion in Crypto Liquidations Hit Markets
items.summary: Leveraged positions were wiped out across Bitcoin and Ethereum, with more than 1 billion dollars in liquidations reported in the last 24 hours. BTC accounted for the bulk of the forced closures amid falling prices and high funding rates. This flush can reset leverage but often signals capitulation that keeps volatility elevated for traders.
items.impact: Forces deleveraging and can accelerate short-term declines

items.title: Bitcoin Trades Near $59,000 Amid Risk-Off Mood
items.summary: Bitcoin opened Friday around 59,700 dollars and slipped further, closing the session near or below 59,000 amid broader market caution. June has seen roughly 18 percent declines so far as capital rotates elsewhere. Traders care because breaking key psychological levels often triggers stop runs and forces reassessment of positions.
items.impact: Maintains downward bias and tests support zones

items.title: Kashkari Shifts to Expect One Fed Rate Hike in 2026
items.summary: Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari told an Aspen panel on Friday he has updated his outlook and now sees one interest rate increase by year-end, citing persistent inflation pressures from tariffs and other factors. He previously expected a cut. Traders should watch this hawkish pivot from a key voter for clues on the Fed's next moves and potential dollar strength.
items.impact: Could support higher yields and pressure risk assets like Bitcoin.

items.title: US Goods Trade Deficit Widens Sharply in May
items.summary: The advanced US goods trade balance came in at a worse-than-expected minus $105.8 billion for May, compared to consensus around minus $85 billion. Retail and wholesale inventory data also released showed modest gains. These figures highlight ongoing trade imbalances that could influence dollar flows and Fed policy thinking.
items.impact: Mixed signals on growth and inflation, limited immediate market reaction on weekend.

items.title: Reuters Poll: Economists See Fed Holding Rates Steady in 2026
items.summary: A fresh Reuters survey of economists finds over three-quarters expect the Federal Reserve to keep rates unchanged through the end of the year, up from prior polls, even as markets price in possible hikes. This comes days after the June FOMC held steady at 3.5-3.75 percent. Traders should note the gap between economist and market views on policy path.
items.impact: Suggests limited near-term rate volatility but highlights policy uncertainty.

items.title: US Consumer Sentiment Final Reading Improves in June
items.summary: The final University of Michigan consumer sentiment index for June printed at 49.5, above expectations and prior readings. The data points to slightly better household confidence amid mixed economic signals. Crypto traders monitor sentiment as a proxy for risk appetite and spending trends.
items.impact: Mild positive for consumer-driven growth outlook.

items.title: Fed Speakers and Data Releases Light on Weekend
items.summary: With US markets closed for the weekend, focus remains on Friday's inventory builds, trade figures, and Kashkari comments rather than new releases. No major central bank decisions or high-impact data like CPI or jobs are scheduled for Saturday or Sunday. Bond yields and DXY showed little movement into the weekend.
items.impact: Quiet period likely keeps markets range-bound until Monday.

items.title: US Strikes Iranian Missile Sites After Hormuz Ship Attack
items.summary: The US military launched strikes on Iranian missile and drone facilities along the Strait of Hormuz and Qeshm Island on Friday in retaliation for an Iranian drone hit on a commercial cargo ship the day before. President Trump called the Iranian action a foolish violation of the fragile ceasefire. The limited strikes target storage and radar sites in a bid to deter further escalation while talks on a broader deal continue. Traders should watch for any fresh disruption to oil flows through the critical waterway.
items.impact: Heightens Middle East tensions and risks renewed oil price volatility.

items.title: Venezuela Quake Death Toll Tops 920 as Rescue Efforts Stall
items.summary: Twin powerful earthquakes that struck Venezuela on Wednesday have now killed at least 920 people with thousands injured or missing. Rescue teams face aftershocks and a lack of heavy equipment three days later while international aid arrives. The disaster hits a key oil-producing country and could complicate regional energy supply dynamics. Traders should monitor any impact on Venezuelan crude output.
items.impact: Potential minor disruption to oil supply from an already strained producer.

items.title: Israel and Lebanon Sign US-Mediated Framework Agreement
items.summary: Israel and Lebanon signed a framework deal in Washington on Friday after days of US-brokered talks. The agreement outlines steps toward Hezbollah disarmament, Lebanese sovereignty restoration, and phased Israeli withdrawals from parts of southern Lebanon. US officials called it the first step toward a broader peace. Markets may see this as a modest de-escalation signal in the Middle East.
items.impact: Supports lower geopolitical risk premium in energy markets.
